thread:
sam: also could be KV cache for headers not keyed per-client. Async event loop/sharing might expose the bug. we should check client._auth_provider vs module-level.

kevin: tagging this for py-sdk auth triage. can someone open a GH issue with 'py-sdk' and 'auth' labels? include minimal repro and logs.

olivia: I'll take it. plan: add unit test that creates two AsyncClients with different env values and asserts different auth headers, then change module cache to be client-scoped. will also test sync path to be safe.

maria: thanks! i'm happy to help with test harness. server logs attached: request IDs r12345 (client_a) and r12346 (client_b) — both show key-A.

ci-bot: CI: queued 1 job for branch olivia/py-sdk-auth-fix.

kevin: nice. olivia, if you need design input, ping me. once fixed we should add a short DX note in the migration guide about client-scoped providers and key rotation best-practices. :memo:

olivia: will do. proposed internal API: AsyncClient(api_key=None, auth_provider=None) where provider gets evaluated per-instance. also add a clear_cached_provider() convenience for rotation usecases.

maria: workaround for anyone hitting this today: pass api_key explicitly or restart process after rotating env var.

jordan: great, thanks. label PR with 'breaking-change?'? might be non-breaking if we keep current behaviour for single-client flows.

olivia: yeah, non-breaking. just moving cache scope. will include changelog entry. :shipit:

maria: thanks team! will follow the PR and retest on our app once merged.
